# Behind the scenes

The MVP platform requirements every story relies on and no screen shows directly.

## Sign-in

User accounts, invites, passwords, and sessions.

<a id="req-identity-0001"></a>

### Hold User accounts and sign in with email and password

`REQ-IDENTITY-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User, Agency User, Iris
- **What:** Every person who uses Iris has their own User, with an email, a name, and an optional phone. They sign in with email and password, and each sign-in is a Session that every later request is checked against.
- **Why:**
  - MSP task: profile and password management *(PLT-4: User accounts with login, profiles and password management)*
  - Each persona gets its own view *(PLT-1: RBAC: unit (buyer), agency (supplier), corporate/program owner)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-4; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-1

**Rules**

- **R1.** A User belongs to one person and holds an email, a first name, a last name, an optional phone, and an active flag.
- **R2.** The email is the sign-in name, and creating a User with an email another User holds is refused.
- **R3.** A phone is accepted when exactly 10 digits remain after spaces, dashes, dots, parentheses, and a leading +1 or 1 are removed; any other value is refused.
- **R4.** A password has at least 12 characters, and only its hash is stored.
- **R5.** Sign-in succeeds only when the email matches an active User and the password matches that User's hash; otherwise it is refused and no Session is created.
- **R6.** A successful sign-in creates a Session for that User, returns its token while storing only the token's hash, and sets last_signed_in_at.
- **R7.** A Session is open from sign-in until the User signs out, which sets ended_at, or until 12 hours have passed since its last accepted request.
- **R8.** A request that needs a signed-in User is accepted only with the token of an open Session whose User is active, which sets last_active_at; otherwise it is refused.
- **R10.** At each start, when no User holds the deployment configuration's email, Iris creates the first Instawork Admin as an active User from the configured email, first name, last name, and password, with no inviter.
- **R11.** Creating or changing a User is recorded in the Audit Trail without the password hash, and Sessions and sign-ins are not recorded there.
- **R12.** A caller may store a context on an open Session, replacing any earlier one, and gets it back with every request; IDENTITY never reads it, and a new Session starts with none.
- **R13.** A start never changes or reactivates a User who already holds the configured email, and [`REQ-ORG-0005`](business-rules.md#req-org-0005) adds that User's INSTAWORK_ADMIN grant when it holds none.
- **R14.** Every other User is created by an invite through [`REQ-IDENTITY-0002`](#req-identity-0002).
- **R15.** When R10 would create the User and the configured email, first name, or last name is missing, or the password has fewer than 12 characters, Iris does not start and says which.

<a id="req-identity-0002"></a>

### Invite a User and reset a password by emailed link

`REQ-IDENTITY-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** A User is added by an invite: Iris creates the User and emails a single-use link to set a password. A User who forgets their password gets a single-use reset link by email.
- **Why:** MSP task: profile and password management *(PLT-4: User accounts with login, profiles and password management)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-4

**Rules**

- **R1.** An invite names the person's email, first name, last name, and optional phone, and the signed-in User who invites them; the calling requirement checks that this User may invite them.
- **R2.** An invite for an email no User holds creates an active User without a password, sets invited_by_id and invited_at, and creates an INVITE AccessLink.
- **R3.** An invite for an email an active User already holds changes nothing and returns that User, unless the inviter asks to send it again before it is accepted, which creates a new INVITE link.
- **R4.** Each new link is emailed to its User as USER_INVITED for an invite or PASSWORD_RESET for a reset, passed to [`REQ-MESSAGING-0001`](#req-messaging-0001) as a secret, and opens the page of [`REQ-SHELL-0005`](every-user.md#req-shell-0005).
- **R5.** An AccessLink works once, expires 72 hours after it is created, and stores only a hash of its token; until its email is sent, the token is held only as that Notification's secret.
- **R6.** Creating a link expires the User's earlier unused links of the same purpose.
- **R7.** A link that is unknown, used, expired, or belongs to a deactivated User is refused, and nothing changes.
- **R8.** With a valid link the User sets a password of at least 12 characters, which stores its hash, sets used_at, and sets invite_accepted_at if it was empty.
- **R9.** Anyone can ask for a reset by entering an email; if it belongs to an active User a PASSWORD_RESET link is created, and otherwise nothing is sent.
- **R10.** The reset screen shows the same message whether or not the email belongs to a User.
- **R11.** Setting a password with a PASSWORD_RESET link sets ended_at on each of that User's open Sessions.
- **R12.** Invites, accepted invites, and password changes are recorded in the Audit Trail, never with the password hash or the token.
- **R13.** An invite for an email a deactivated User holds is refused, and the refusal says that User is deactivated and must be reactivated before being invited or granted a role.

<a id="req-identity-0003"></a>

### Let a User change their own name and phone

`REQ-IDENTITY-0003`

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** A signed-in User sees their own User and changes their own first name, last name, and phone. The email cannot be changed, and the password changes only by a reset link.
- **Why:** MSP task: profile and password management *(PLT-4: User accounts with login, profiles and password management)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-4

**Rules**

- **R1.** A signed-in User can read their own email, first name, last name, and phone, and never a password hash.
- **R2.** A signed-in User can change their own first name, last name, and phone, and no other User's.
- **R3.** Nobody can change a User's email, and a password changes only through an emailed reset link, never on the profile.
- **R4.** A first or last name cannot be saved empty, a phone is checked as [`REQ-IDENTITY-0001`](#req-identity-0001) checks it, and saving the phone empty clears it.
- **R5.** Each change is recorded in the Audit Trail as an UPDATE made by that User.

<a id="req-identity-0004"></a>

### Deactivate and reactivate a User

`REQ-IDENTITY-0004` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Agency User
- **What:** A User who should no longer use Iris is deactivated, which ends their access at once and keeps their records. Reactivating gives the same User their access back.
- **Why:** MSP task: profile and password management *(PLT-4: User accounts with login, profiles and password management)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) PLT-4

**Rules**

- **R1.** Deactivating a User sets is_active to false and sets ended_at on each of their open Sessions, so their next request is refused.
- **R2.** The caller checks who may deactivate or reactivate whom, as [`REQ-ORG-0005`](business-rules.md#req-org-0005) states, and this requirement makes no such check.
- **R3.** Reactivating sets is_active to true and restores no Session, so the User signs in again with the password they had.
- **R4.** Neither action changes anything else: the User's password, invite, Role Grants, and other records stay as they were.
- **R5.** Deactivating an inactive User, or reactivating an active one, changes nothing and records nothing.
- **R6.** Each deactivation and reactivation is recorded in the Audit Trail as an UPDATE of active made by the acting User.

## Agent runtime

Rules every AI-assisted flow follows: interpret with the LLM, compute with code, wait for approval.

<a id="req-agent-0001"></a>

### Interpret with the LLM, compute with code

`REQ-AGENT-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Every call to the LLM goes through one gateway, which reads typed requests, column names, and text in files, and writes summaries and explanations. Code does every validation check, every match, and all money and hours math. The one exception is the AI check of credential documents.
- **Why:** Fraudulent certificates are a concern *(WA-15: AI document validation: checks expiry, issuer, signs of editing, and public registries where available)*
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 What the LLM does and what code does; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-15

**Rules**

- **R1.** The LLM is used only to read typed requests, column names, and text in files and messages, and to write summaries, questions, and explanations.
- **R2.** Every validation check, every match to a stored record, and all money and hours math is done by code, never by the LLM.
- **R3.** Given the same values read from a file or request and the same user decisions, code returns the same checks, matches, and amounts every time.
- **R4.** LLM output never changes a record directly: it becomes values in a Proposal, a question, or an answer to the user.
- **R5.** Credential document checks are the exception: the model reads each document file and returns its issuer, its dates, and any signs of editing, and [`REQ-COMPLIANCE-0003`](business-rules.md#req-compliance-0003) saves the result without a Proposal.
- **R6.** Every call to the LLM goes through this requirement, which alone holds the provider.
- **R7.** A reading returns a value for each field asked for, empty where the text or file gives none; output in any other shape, or no answer, is returned as a failure, never as a guess.
- **R8.** This requirement reads and changes no record but its own LlmCall log, so whatever the LLM returns reaches a record only through its caller's own rules.
- **R9.** A caller passes a text, or a PDF or image file, and the fields to read from it, or the facts to put into words.
- **R10.** Every call saves one LlmCall with its caller, purpose, model, acting User, channel, the record read, the input and output text, token counts, duration, outcome, and any error.
- **R11.** A daily job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](#req-jobs-0001) clears the input and output text of each LlmCall older than 90 days and sets text_cleared_at, keeping the rest.
- **R12.** LlmCall records are for Instawork engineering to debug and evaluate the agents, and no Iris screen or role lists them.

- [`REQ-ASSISTANT-0003` Hand each typed request to the requirement that owns it](every-user.md#req-assistant-0003)

<a id="req-agent-0002"></a>

### Save nothing until a person approves the Proposal

`REQ-AGENT-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User, Agency User, Iris
- **What:** Every change Iris prepares from a file or a message is a Proposal that lists each proposed change, any problem found, and a suggested fix. Nothing is saved until the person it was made for approves it, and each accepted item is rechecked as it is saved.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Agent Chat

**Rules**

- **R1.** A Proposal is created OPEN with its kind, its channel, the User it was made for, a summary, and one ProposalItem for each proposed change.
- **R2.** Each ProposalItem holds its action, record type, and values, and one entry for each problem a check found: the field it is on, a message, and any fix or candidates.
- **R3.** While a Proposal is OPEN it has changed no record other than itself and its ProposalItems.
- **R4.** Only the User the Proposal was made for can decide it, and only while it is OPEN; any other attempt is refused.
- **R5.** That User sets each item's decision to ACCEPTED, to EDITED with the values as they leave them, or to REJECTED, and can accept at once every undecided item that can be ACCEPTED.
- **R6.** ACCEPTED puts each fix's value into field_values and is refused while a problem has neither a fix nor a picked candidate; EDITED applies no fix and keeps the User's values, changed or not.
- **R7.** The User then applies the Proposal: an undecided item with no problem counts as ACCEPTED, and applying is refused while an item with a problem has no decision.
- **R8.** On apply, the ACCEPTED and EDITED items are handed, in list order, to the save step of the Proposal's kind, whose owner rechecks each item against its own rules at that moment.
- **R9.** An item its owner saves gets result SAVED and the saved record's id in record_id; an item its owner refuses is not saved and gets FAILED_RECHECK with the owner's reason in result_message.
- **R10.** A REJECTED item is never saved and gets no result.
- **R11.** After apply the Proposal is APPLIED when every ACCEPTED or EDITED item is SAVED, and PARTLY_APPLIED when at least one is FAILED_RECHECK.
- **R12.** Rejecting the Proposal, or applying it with every item REJECTED, sets every item REJECTED and the Proposal REJECTED, and saves nothing.
- **R13.** Deciding sets decided_by_id and decided_at, and a decided Proposal never changes again, so a failed item is retried only in a new Proposal.
- **R14.** Each save is given the Proposal's id and channel and the deciding User, so the Audit Trail shows where the change came from.
- **R15.** An OPEN Proposal does not expire: it stays OPEN until its User decides it.
- **R16.** A User can list the Proposals made for them, OPEN ones first, and no one else's.
- **R17.** Accepting an item that has a fix which drops it, such as a duplicate row, sets its decision to REJECTED, and setting it EDITED keeps it.
- **R18.** An item's values are one flat set of names and values: for FILE_ROWS the names are the upload type's catalog columns, and for any other kind the requirement that proposes it names them.
- **R19.** Candidates for a name are every stored record that matches it or, when none does, the three stored names closest to it by single-character edits, with ties in alphabetical order.
- **R20.** The User picks at most one candidate for a problem, which stores that candidate's value in picked, and the owner saves the item against the record picked.
- **R21.** Items that share a group_key make one record together, such as the Shifts of one Request, and are handed to the save step in one call.
- **R22.** Each item saves whole or not at all, with its Audit Trail entries and Notifications, and an item that is refused leaves every other item saved, in its group or outside it.
- **R23.** Each Proposal kind has one save step, registered by the requirement that proposes that kind; for FILE_ROWS it is [`REQ-INTAKE-0002`](#req-intake-0002), which hands each row to its upload type's owner.
- **R24.** When a name matches no stored record and exactly one stored name is closest to it, that name is the problem's fix as well as a candidate.
- **R25.** A candidate the User picks replaces the problem's fix, so accepting the item uses the picked record.
- **R26.** A problem on a field whose value lists several names says which entry it is about, and its fix or picked candidate replaces that entry only and leaves the others as they are.

<a id="req-agent-0003"></a>

### Ask when unsure, and refuse data the user does not own

`REQ-AGENT-0003` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Before proposing anything, Iris asks when it cannot tell what a file or request is, or when details are missing. When a user sends data their role may not send, Iris says who owns it and saves nothing.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 When the agent is unsure; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads

**Rules**

- **R1.** When a file or message could be more than one upload type or kind of request, Iris asks the user which it is and creates no Proposal until they answer.
- **R2.** When a typed request lacks a detail the change needs, such as a date, a time, or a headcount, Iris asks for it before creating a Proposal.
- **R3.** Who may send each upload type is the uploaders list for that type in the upload-types catalog, checked against the role the User is acting in, which the caller supplies.
- **R4.** When that role is not among the type's uploaders, such as a Unit User sending a RATE_CARD, Iris names the roles that may send it, creates no Proposal, and saves nothing.
- **R5.** For a typed request, the requirement that owns the change says whether the User may make it; if not, Iris says who can and creates no Proposal.
- **R6.** A question or a refusal is given on the channel the file or message arrived on.
- **R7.** A question goes back to the caller with what was understood so far, and the caller returns the answer with it; this requirement keeps nothing between the two.

- [`REQ-ASSISTANT-0003` Hand each typed request to the requirement that owns it](every-user.md#req-assistant-0003)

## File intake

Files in and out: type detection, row validation, templates, the upload log, and CSV downloads.

<a id="req-intake-0001"></a>

### Accept a file and detect its upload type

`REQ-INTAKE-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Program User, Unit User, Agency User, Iris
- **What:** A User sends a CSV, Excel, PDF, or image file on the Uploads page, in the assistant, or attached to a message. Iris stores it privately, detects its upload type from the catalog, and asks when it cannot tell. It also keeps and serves the files other requirements store, such as a Worker's photo.
- **Why:** Most temp time is on paper today; only about 2% runs through MyStaff *(TS-5: Timesheet intake in any format (PDF, CSV, image), matched to shifts automatically)*
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 Agent Chat; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) TS-5

**Rules**

- **R1.** Each file sent creates one Upload with status RECEIVED, its file name, the User who sent it, and the channel it arrived on: APP, ASSISTANT, EMAIL, or SMS.
- **R2.** The original file is kept unchanged in private storage, and file_url is never a public link.
- **R3.** CSV and Excel files are accepted for every upload type except CREDENTIALS, and PDF and image files only for TIMESHEETS, TIPS, EXPENSES, and CREDENTIALS; any other pairing of file and picked type becomes FAILED.
- **R4.** Text in a PDF or an image is read by OCR before the type is detected.
- **R5.** When the uploader picked a type, it is used; otherwise the LLM maps the file's column names to the catalog columns of every registered upload type that takes CSV and Excel, and code chooses one.
- **R6.** When detection chooses one type, the Upload's type is set; when no type fits or the best ones tie, the status becomes NEEDS_TYPE and the uploader is asked to pick one.
- **R7.** When the uploader picks a type for a NEEDS_TYPE Upload, the type is set and the status returns to RECEIVED.
- **R8.** If the role the uploader is acting in, which the caller supplies, is not among the type's uploaders, the Upload becomes FAILED and failure_reason names the roles that may send that type.
- **R9.** A file that cannot be opened, is not a CSV, Excel, PDF, or image file, or holds no rows or readable text becomes FAILED, with failure_reason saying why.
- **R10.** A type fits a file that holds every column of one of its identified_by sets in the catalog, or every column marked required yes when the type lists no set.
- **R11.** For a PDF or an image, the LLM names the one upload type the OCR text holds, among the registered ones of TIMESHEETS, TIPS, EXPENSES, and CREDENTIALS, or none, which makes the Upload NEEDS_TYPE.
- **R12.** A file larger than 10 MB is refused when it is sent and creates no Upload, and a file with more than 5,000 rows becomes FAILED.
- **R13.** Excel means an .xlsx workbook and an image a JPEG or PNG file; the first row that holds a value is the header, and a workbook with rows on more than one sheet becomes FAILED.
- **R14.** The requirement that owns an upload type registers it, with its check step and its save step, when it is delivered, and until then the type is neither offered to pick nor detected.
- **R15.** Among the types that fit a file, the one that covers the most of the file's columns is chosen.
- **R16.** A requirement may store a PDF, JPEG, or PNG file of at most 10 MB without creating an Upload, such as a Worker's photo, and gets back its private reference.
- **R17.** A stored file, an Upload's or not, is read only through this requirement, by the requirement that holds its reference or by a signed-in User whom that requirement says may see it.

<a id="req-intake-0002"></a>

### Validate every row and propose fixes

`REQ-INTAKE-0002` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris reads every row of an Upload, checks it against the catalog's columns and its owner's rules, and creates a Proposal with a fix or candidates for each problem. It never changes a value from the file silently.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 What the agent checks

**Rules**

- **R1.** Once an Upload has a type its uploader may send, Iris sets total_rows and creates one FILE_ROWS Proposal for the uploader, with channel FILE_UPLOAD, or EMAIL or SMS when the Upload arrived that way.
- **R2.** The LLM maps the file's column names to the type's columns in the upload-types catalog, and code does every check after that.
- **R3.** For a PDF or an image, the LLM reads the OCR text into rows of the type's catalog columns, and those rows are checked like file rows.
- **R4.** A row with no value in a column the catalog marks required yes has a problem; a column required only under a condition is checked by the type's owner.
- **R5.** A value in template format is accepted as it is: a date as YYYY-MM-DD, a time like 4:00 PM, and money as a number with at most two decimals and no dollar sign.
- **R6.** A date, time, or money value in another known form, such as 10/18/26 or $30, is a problem whose fix is the same value in template format.
- **R7.** The known forms are month-first slash dates, 12-hour and 24-hour times such as 4pm or 16:00, and money with a dollar sign or thousands commas.
- **R8.** A value that cannot be read as its column's kind in the catalog is a problem.
- **R9.** Each lookup the catalog names is resolved by the type's owner, and a value that matches no record or several is a problem carrying the fix and candidates [`REQ-AGENT-0002`](#req-agent-0002) gives for a name.
- **R10.** Checks across columns, across rows, or against stored records belong to the type's owner, which is given every row of the file at once and returns each row's problems for INTAKE to report.
- **R11.** A row the type's owner reports as a duplicate of an earlier row has a problem whose fix is to drop the later row.
- **R12.** Every row becomes one ProposalItem carrying its row_no and one problem entry for each problem found, each naming the catalog column it is on.
- **R13.** No value from the file is changed unless the uploader accepts a fix for it, picks a candidate, or edits it.
- **R14.** Creating the Proposal sets the Upload to IN_REVIEW with proposal_id and rows_to_review, the number of rows that have a problem.
- **R15.** INTAKE calls only the type's owner, to check rows and to save accepted ones, and the owner passes each column with saved_by in the catalog to that requirement, whose rules check and save it.
- **R16.** When the Proposal becomes APPLIED or PARTLY_APPLIED the Upload becomes SAVED, and when it becomes REJECTED the Upload becomes DISCARDED.
- **R17.** A file column the LLM maps to no catalog column of the type is left out of every item, and the Proposal's summary names each column left out.
- **R18.** Rows the type's owner says make one record together, such as the Shifts of one Request, get one group_key on their items.
- **R19.** A text value is kept as written, an int value is a whole number written in digits, and a yes_no value is Yes or No in any letter case.
- **R20.** The type's owner may add a fix to any problem, including one INTAKE found, such as a missing date that the other rows of its group share.
- **R21.** Where the catalog says a column's names are separated by semicolons, each name is looked up on its own, and each that fails is its own problem under [`REQ-AGENT-0002.R26`](#req-agent-0002).

<a id="req-intake-0003"></a>

### Provide a template for each upload type

`REQ-INTAKE-0003`

- **Who:** Program User, Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** Each upload type that takes CSV or Excel has a template whose columns come from the upload-types catalog, downloadable as CSV or Excel. The template is the same on the Uploads page and in the assistant.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Templates; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §7 How it connects

**Rules**

- **R1.** The template for an upload type has one header row holding that type's column names from the upload-types catalog, in catalog order.
- **R2.** A template can be downloaded as CSV or as an Excel .xlsx file, and a filled template is accepted in either format.
- **R3.** A User is offered templates only for the upload types registered under [`REQ-INTAKE-0001`](#req-intake-0001) whose uploaders in the catalog include the role they are acting in, which the caller supplies.
- **R4.** The Uploads page and the assistant give the same template for a type.
- **R5.** Rows added to a template use dates as YYYY-MM-DD, times like 4:00 PM, and money without a dollar sign.
- **R6.** CREDENTIALS has no template, because it takes one document for each Credential and never a CSV or Excel file.

<a id="req-intake-0004"></a>

### Keep a log of every upload

`REQ-INTAKE-0004`

- **Who:** Program User, Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** Every file a User sends is listed in that User's upload log with its type, time, row count, and status. This covers files sent on the Uploads page, in the assistant, and attached to a message.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads

**Rules**

- **R1.** Every Upload appears in the log, whether it was sent on the Uploads page, in the assistant, or attached to an email or text.
- **R2.** A User sees only the Uploads they sent themselves.
- **R3.** Each line shows the file name, type, upload time, total rows, and status, with the newest Upload first.
- **R4.** An IN_REVIEW line shows rows_to_review and opens its Proposal, a NEEDS_TYPE line lets the uploader pick the type, and a FAILED line shows failure_reason.

<a id="req-intake-0005"></a>

### Download any table as CSV

`REQ-INTAKE-0005` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User, Agency User
- **What:** Any table a User sees can be downloaded as a CSV file that holds exactly the rows and columns of that User's view.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §6 Uploads

**Rules**

- **R1.** The requirement that shows a table passes INTAKE the rows and columns the User may see there, and INTAKE adds no rows and no columns.
- **R2.** The file has one header row with the table's column names, then one line per row, with the table's filters and sort applied and every page included.
- **R3.** Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD, times like 4:00 PM, and money without a dollar sign.
- **R4.** A download creates no Upload and changes no record.
- **R5.** A timestamp is written as its date and its time in those formats, in the timezone the table shows it in, which the caller names.

## Messaging

Email, SMS, phone, and in-app messages, outbound and inbound.

<a id="req-messaging-0001"></a>

### Send notifications by email, SMS, and in the app

`REQ-MESSAGING-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Instawork Admin, Program User, Unit User, Agency User, Iris
- **What:** Iris sends each notification type to the recipients its owner names, on the channels the notifications catalog lists for it. It records for every message whether it was sent, failed, or read.
- **Why:**
  - Agencies are half the users; they need to know the moment a shift is theirs *(SC-8: Agency notifications for released shifts (email or SMS), with accept or decline)*
  - VMS requirement: onboarding instructions (attire, directions, parking) *(SC-6: Structured shift instructions shared with the agency and sent to workers by text or email: parking, entrance, directions, site contact, attire)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-8; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-6; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) Overview

**Rules**

- **R1.** The owner of a notification type sends it by naming the type, one record of its catalog subject entity, a title, a body, and the recipients; a type the catalog lacks is refused.
- **R2.** The owner works out who the catalog's recipients are; a recipient is a User, or an email address or phone number for a Worker or other person with no User.
- **R3.** One Notification is created with status QUEUED for each recipient on each channel the catalog lists for the type, or only on those of them the owner names for that send.
- **R4.** EMAIL goes to a User's email and SMS to a User's phone, stored in to_address when the Notification is created, and a channel the recipient has no address for is skipped.
- **R5.** An IN_APP Notification is created only for a User.
- **R6.** When the caller names the User whose action caused the notification, that User gets none; PASSWORD_RESET and INBOUND_REPLY name no such User, because they answer that person.
- **R7.** No Notification is created for a User whose active flag is false.
- **R8.** A secret the caller passes, such as a link, is stored in the secret field, never in body, added to the message when it is sent, and erased when the Notification becomes SENT or FAILED.
- **R9.** An IN_APP Notification becomes SENT, with sent_at, as soon as it is stored.
- **R10.** An EMAIL or SMS Notification is first tried as soon as the change that queued it is saved, and becomes SENT, with sent_at, when the provider accepts it.
- **R11.** An interval job of [`REQ-JOBS-0001`](#req-jobs-0001) tries each EMAIL or SMS Notification still QUEUED; every try adds one to attempts, and the third refusal makes it FAILED with the provider's reason.
- **R12.** A FAILED Notification never undoes or blocks the change that caused it.
- **R13.** A User sees only their own IN_APP Notifications, newest first, and opening one sets read_at once.
- **R14.** The title is the email's subject line and the inbox heading, and a text carries the body only; the owner words both in plain text from the facts its own rule names.
- **R15.** A try the provider does not answer counts as a refusal, and failure_reason then says the provider did not answer.
- **R16.** When the provider accepts an email, the message id it gives is stored in provider_message_id, so [`REQ-MESSAGING-0002`](#req-messaging-0002) can tell which message a reply answers.

<a id="req-messaging-0002"></a>

### Receive requests by email, SMS, and phone

`REQ-MESSAGING-0002`

- **Who:** Program User, Unit User, Agency User, Iris
- **What:** Iris has an email address, an SMS number, and a phone line answered by an AI voice agent. It matches each sender to a User, passes what they ask to the requirement that takes requests by message, and answers on the same channel.
- **Why:** About 30% of Instawork shifts already come in through chat *(SC-10: Booking by email, SMS and phone through an AI agent, with memory of each unit's preferences)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) SC-10

**Rules**

- **R1.** Every email, text, and call Iris receives is stored as one InboundMessage with its channel, sender, body, and received time.
- **R2.** A call is answered by an AI voice agent and stored as one InboundMessage when it begins, and its body is set to the transcript of both sides when the call ends.
- **R3.** An email matches the active User whose email equals the sender's address, and a text or call the active User whose phone equals the sender's number, each compared in its stored form.
- **R4.** When exactly one User matches, user_id is set; otherwise it stays empty and no Upload or Proposal is created.
- **R5.** Each attachment of a message the handling requirement accepts becomes an Upload through [`REQ-INTAKE-0001`](#req-intake-0001), sent by the matched User in the acting role it supplies, on the message's channel, and linked as an attachment.
- **R6.** Each matched message that decides no Proposal goes to the handling requirement, [`REQ-ORDERING-0010`](business-rules.md#req-ordering-0010) in MVP, which supplies the sender's acting role and context and returns a question, a Proposal, or a refusal.
- **R7.** An email replying to a stored message joins its thread, a text joins the sender's last text thread if that had a message in the past 24 hours, and anything else starts one.
- **R8.** A reply in a thread, from the User its one OPEN Proposal was made for, applies that Proposal when it is an approval and rejects it when it is a refusal.
- **R9.** Iris answers each email or text with an INBOUND_REPLY to the sender, naming the message's channel so it goes out on that channel only; on a call the voice agent answers aloud instead.
- **R10.** The Proposal a message's words lead to is stored in its proposal_id, and a thread's Proposals are those of its messages and of the Uploads attached to them.
- **R11.** Approval by reply accepts every item and applies the Proposal through [`REQ-AGENT-0002`](#req-agent-0002); when an item cannot be ACCEPTED, or the thread has several OPEN Proposals, Iris answers that it is decided in the app.
- **R12.** A reply that is neither an approval nor a refusal is passed on as a new message in the thread, so it can answer a question or change the request.
- **R13.** On a call the voice agent says only what these rules produce: it asks each question aloud, reads a Proposal's summary aloud, and takes a spoken yes or no as the reply.
- **R14.** A Proposal still OPEN when a call ends or a thread goes quiet stays OPEN, and its User decides it in the app or by a later reply.
- **R15.** When the handling requirement refuses the sender or the request, Iris answers with its reason and creates no Upload and no Proposal.
- **R16.** An unmatched caller is told aloud, on every call, that Iris does not recognize the number, and the call then ends.
- **R17.** An email replies to a stored message when the message id it answers equals the provider_message_id of an InboundMessage, or of an INBOUND_REPLY, whose subject is the InboundMessage it answered.
- **R18.** Code decides: a reply is an approval when its own text, without quoted earlier messages, punctuation, and case, is yes, approve, or confirm, and a refusal when it is no, reject, or cancel.
- **R19.** An answer that carries a Proposal tells the sender to reply yes to approve it or no to reject it.
- **R20.** On a call, each thing the caller says is passed to the handling requirement as it is said, as a message in the call's thread is, and the answer is spoken.
- **R21.** A call ends when the caller hangs up, or when the caller has said nothing for 30 seconds.
- **R22.** Iris tells an unmatched email or text sender, at most once in 24 hours for one address or number, that it does not recognize them.

## Audit trail

Append-only history of who changed what.

<a id="req-audit-0001"></a>

### Record who changed what

`REQ-AUDIT-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Every change to a product record or a User goes into an append-only Audit Trail: who made it, when, through which channel, the old and new values, and the reason. Nobody can change or delete an entry.
- **Why:**
  - Know who changed a rate, when and why *(RC-5: Rate change audit trail)*
  - Agencies attest; Compass audits *(WA-16: Attestation records and audit trail for agency-worker compliance (audited by Compass or the MSP))*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) RC-5; [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-16; [PRD](https://instawork.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ec/pages/4841898227/Compass+VMS+Product+Requirements) §2 Shifts

**Rules**

- **R1.** Every create, update, and delete of a product record or a User writes one AuditEvent together with the change, and if the event cannot be written the change is not saved.
- **R2.** No product record is exempt: Role Grants, Agency approvals, Releases, Worker ratings, Tip Pools, and expenses are audited in the same way as rates, Shifts, and Timesheets.
- **R3.** An AuditEvent holds the record's entity name and id, the action, the acting User, the channel, and the time; actor_id is empty only when Iris itself made the change.
- **R4.** For an UPDATE, old_values and new_values hold the fields that changed; a CREATE holds the whole record in new_values only, and a DELETE holds it in old_values only.
- **R5.** The channel says how the change reached Iris: APP, FILE_UPLOAD, ASSISTANT, EMAIL, SMS, PHONE, API, or SYSTEM.
- **R6.** A change saved from a Proposal carries that Proposal's id and channel on its AuditEvent.
- **R7.** When the requirement making a change requires a reason, the reason is stored on the AuditEvent.
- **R8.** No User of any role, and no other part of Iris, can change or delete an AuditEvent.
- **R9.** Proposals, Uploads, Notifications, InboundMessages, AccessLinks, Sessions, and sign-in times are not audited, and a password hash or link token is never stored in old_values or new_values.
- **R10.** The AuditEvents of one record can be listed newest first, and the requirement that shows them decides which Users may see them.
- **R11.** Deactivating, reactivating, revoking, cancelling, or any other change that keeps the record is an UPDATE, and a DELETE is recorded only when the record itself is removed.

## Scheduled work

Runs the work that happens when a time passes or each day, on time and once.

<a id="req-jobs-0001"></a>

### Run scheduled work on time and once

`REQ-JOBS-0001` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris runs the work requirements schedule, such as a sweep after a Shift starts or a daily check, at most five minutes late and never twice at once. The requirement that schedules a job owns what it does.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** Graph seven MVP requirements act when a time passes, and none provides the clock

**Rules**

- **R1.** A requirement registers a job with a name and either a five-minute interval, or a daily local time with one timezone or with a step that lists the timezones to run in.
- **R2.** An interval job runs every five minutes, and a daily job runs once for each of its timezones and local dates, at the first run at or after its local time on that date.
- **R3.** A timed rule takes effect at the first run at or after its time, so it is at most five minutes late; a run that fails is retried at the next run.
- **R4.** Only one run of a job is in progress at a time, even with several servers, and a run repeated for the same time changes nothing the first run already changed.
- **R6.** A daily job for something that belongs to no Unit, such as a Credential, uses the program timezone, America/New_York.
- **R7.** On a day the clocks skip a daily job's local time the job runs at the first run after the skip, and on a day they repeat it, at the first occurrence only.
- **R8.** Each daily run saves a JobRun for its job, timezone, and local date together with the run's changes, and a run whose JobRun already exists is not made.
- **R9.** A job's timezone step is called at every run, so a timezone that Units newly have is covered from then on without registering the job again.
- **R10.** A daily run is made only on its own local date, so a date that passes with no run at or after the job's local time gets none later.

- [D-67](open-questions.md#d-67) How often does timed work run?

## Integrations

Connections to Compass, Agency, and verification systems.

<a id="req-integrations-0006"></a>

### Verify a credential with its issuer

`REQ-INTEGRATIONS-0006` · first slice

- **Who:** Iris
- **What:** Iris checks a credential with its issuer or a public registry where one is connected, and returns the result with a reference. Where none is connected the check is skipped.
- **Why:** Fraudulent certificates are a concern *(WA-15: AI document validation: checks expiry, issuer, signs of editing, and public registries where available)*
- **Sources:** [Compass sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SlUyWtbhik3KEKW4VAskSAEfS8v3S-_OjgVfZpA2WM4/edit) WA-15; [Demo sessions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy3QVWr-aVVV6mpMxWsH6kb987IzwVPXDQ1iW8k83Bo/edit) Worker Assignment & Compliance

**Rules**

- **R1.** The caller passes the credential's type, issuer, number, holder name, and dates, and Iris asks the issuer or public registry connected for it whether the credential is valid.
- **R2.** The result is confirmed when the source says the credential is valid, not confirmed when it says it is not valid or cannot find it, and otherwise not available.
- **R3.** A confirmed or not confirmed result carries the name of the source and the reference it gave.
- **R4.** When no issuer or registry is connected for the credential, or the source does not answer, the result is not available and the caller relies on its document checks alone.
- **R5.** MVP connects no issuer and no registry, so every result is not available until Compass names the providers it relies on (I-6) and one is connected.

**Open questions it rests on**

<a id="req-integrations-0009"></a>

### Keep the ids other systems use for Iris records

`REQ-INTEGRATIONS-0009`

- **Who:** Instawork Admin
- **What:** Iris keeps the id that Compass's Fieldglass, SAP, or MyStaff uses for a Company, Unit, Department, Agency, or Position. Loads, migrations, and Iris's agents match records across systems by these ids instead of by name.
- **Why:** Not given in Compass's sheet; the sources below are where it comes from.
- **Sources:** Graph compass-vms-dashboard maps Fieldglass cost center codes to Instawork Company, Business, and region ids

**Rules**

- **R1.** An Instawork Admin records, changes, or removes the id one ExternalSystem uses for one Iris record.
- **R2.** Ids are kept only for Companies, Units, Departments, Agencies, and Positions, and record_type names that entity.
- **R3.** A record has at most one id per system, and two records of one type never share an id in one system; a repeat is refused and names the record that holds it.
- **R4.** An id is stored exactly as the outside system writes it, with only leading and trailing spaces removed.
- **R5.** No Iris rule needs an id to be present; an id only matches a record to the same record in that system.

**Screens that use it**

- [`REQ-ADMIN-WEB-0006` Keep the ids other systems use for Iris records](instawork-admin.md#req-admin-web-0006)
